messages:
sam: quick heads-up — I ran a focused nsys + perfetto trace on the microbatch coalescer change in canary. Seeing intermittent tail queue spikes on p99 requests after coalescing.
anya: how big are the coalesced microbatches when spikes happen?
sam: usually 6-8 small requests got merged into an 8 microbatch. Baseline (no coalesce) had many size=1/2 kernels but no 20-60ms queue waits.
devon: that sounds like kernel-selection churn. If we cross the kernel threshold from small->med, we might be doing a different matmul kernel that has higher launch latency + setup.
sam: exactly. Snippet from perfetto timeline (filtered):
```
0.0s  -> enqueue request A
+2ms   -> enqueue requests B..G
+5ms   -> coalescer emits batch size=8
+6ms   -> kernel launch (cutlass_gemm_variant_B) 34.2ms
queue delay measured before launch: 22.4ms (host-side spin / prefetch backoff)
KV cache sweep fired at +18ms, added another 8ms stall
```
luis: do we have NVTX tags showing which kernel variant was chosen? can we correlate with sequence length or kv cache hit patterns?
sam: NVTX shows variant_B chosen whenever effective_seq_len >= 512 OR batch_size >= 6. Many of these tiny requests have longer context so coalescer pushes them over the variant threshold.
mei: possible root causes:
- kernel variant thresholds are too coarse -> thrash when mixed microbatches
- coalescer doesn't respect kv-cache locality -> a batch with mixed cache states triggers sweeps
- host-side batching timing creates a long tail before flush
anya: can you post the exact nsys command and the short output that flagged the hotspot?
sam: ran: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -o microbatch-coal` then pulled timeline + top CUDA stacks. Top line showed repeated cuLaunchKernel gaps:
```
cuLaunchKernel gap histogram: 0-2ms: 72%, 2-10ms: 18%, 10-60ms: 10% (tail)
Kernel runtimes stable, but launch gaps correlate with coalescer flush points
```
devon: quick hypothesis — when we emit larger mixed-effect batches we hit a different kernel and also trigger a KV sweep on the GPU memory manager because of an eviction pattern. Sweep blocks host for a bit.
luis: to validate: 1) run same workload forcing coalescer to flush earlier (max_batch_age=1ms) 2) run with kernel-selection disabled (force small kernel) 3) run with KV sweep disabled in runtime (debug flag)
sam: ran 1) and 2) in canary: forcing earlier flush removed the 20-60ms queue tail, but increased overall token cost slightly. Forcing small kernel removed the tail entirely but showed degraded overall throughput.
mei: that's useful — it's a tradeoff (latency vs throughput). We should consider making coalescer kernel-aware: avoid growing a batch across kernel-selection boundaries unless latency budget allows.
anya: also add a quick guard: if a batch contains requests with different kv-cache states (mix of cold/warm), prefer flushing to avoid sweep coupling.
devon: agree. Action items:
- sam: attach perfetto link + trimmed nsys csv to the ticket (investigation) — include NVTX spans. (ETA today)
- luis: prototype a kernel-aware coalescer policy (simple threshold where coalescer won't merge across variant boundary) — bench tomorrow
- mei: add runtime flag to disable KV sweep during coalescer flush or make it async — spike next week
perf-bot: trace uploaded: https://perf.internal/traces/microbatch-coal-2087654321 :white_check_mark:
sam: uploaded logs + small timeline clip to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2042 — comments summarise the tradeoffs.
anya: cool. let's sync briefly after luis' bench. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
